drugRefs.why: First-line for uncomplicated cystitis - narrow urinary-tract-specific spectrum, low resistance rates, and minimal collateral ecological damage compared to broader agents.

drugRefs.coverage: Effective alternative where local E. coli resistance is <20%; check local resistance data before use.
Single-dose option useful for adherence concerns; broad activity against typical uropathogens.

coverageMatrix.completeness: Covers the majority of uncomplicated cystitis pathogens with a narrow, urine-concentrated agent.
gaps: Not effective for upper tract infection - not used if pyelonephritis is suspected, since it doesn't achieve adequate tissue levels.

stewardship.deescalation: Not typically needed given short empiric courses; if symptoms persist beyond 48-72 hours, obtain urine culture and adjust based on susceptibility.

framework: Avoid fluoroquinolones as first-line for uncomplicated cystitis - reserve for complicated infection or treatment failure.
Routine urine culture is not required before starting empiric therapy in a straightforward, non-pregnant, non-complicated presentation.
Use the shortest effective duration (3-5 days) rather than longer courses, which do not improve cure rates but increase resistance pressure.
